Compliance with 24-Hour Primary and Secondary Air Quality Standards
The most important concern with respect to the effect of the demolition process on ambient air quality is the level of TSP experienced by the nearest receptors. The proposed demolitions involve receptors in the area immediately adjacent to the dust generating activities. The ground level origin of the dust will cause the highest ambient TSP concentrations to occur at the location of the closest downwind receptors. The sampling sites used in this study serve the dual function of providing ambient air quality measurements at the closest receptors in the vicinity, and allowing for estimates of the dust generation rate from the source. The results, in effect, supply the most significant information that could have been obtained from diffusion models, were they applicable to these source-receptor configurations.
When related to the 24-hour ambient air quality standards for suspended particulates, the values measured in this study are extremely high. However, the significance of this impact is tempered by several important considerations:
1. Given the configuration of the site, the most significant impact is confined to the receptors in the vicinity of the demolition activity. Although these particulate levels are high, they will not be experienced by the majority of the metropolitan area population.
2. The duration of the impact is limited to the duration of an individual demolition, or about 2 days per site.
3. The size distribution of particulates indicates that there will be a major soiling impact and some risk to health, although this cannot be quantified. The respirable component of the particulates accounts for approximately 10 percent of the total emissions.
5. Control procedures, i.e., continuous wetting and scheduling, will reduce TSP levels by a minimum of 80 percent.
6. The demolition activity can be scheduled so that it need not take place during periods of adverse meteorological conditions. If D.E.Q.E. would like to see demolition activity suspended during adverse meteorological conditions, it should notify the Office of Community Development when these conditions occur.
